=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:117 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case statement accepts `identical|ahead` when comparing `${DISPATCH_SHA}...${STABLE_TIP}`, rejecting a legitimate dispatched SHA that is an ancestor of the live stable tip and accepting a dispatched SHA not in stable's history.
  WHY: A dispatched old tip that is an ancestor of the live tip returns `behind` and is rejected; a dispatched SHA ahead of stable returns `ahead` and passes.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:248 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case accepts `identical|ahead` when it must accept `identical|behind`.
  WHY: Legitimate dispatched SHAs that are ancestors of the stable tip are rejected, while an untrusted SHA ahead of stable can pass verification.
- tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py:423, 429 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test asserts that `ahead` passes and `behind` fails, encoding the reversed logic.
  WHY: When production code is fixed to accept `behind` instead of `ahead`, this test will fail.
- Requirement: "Verify the dispatched SHA against the stable branch before exposing release credentials or executing checked-out code."
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:65-124 and .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:195-255 (the Verify dispatched commit is on stable step)
  Evidence of absence: The verification steps exist but the compare direction is reversed. `identical|ahead` at lines mark-stable.yml:117 and test-and-mark-stable.yml:248 passes untrusted commits ahead of stable and rejects legitimate ancestors. The existing confirmation pattern in `scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:185` uses the correct `identical|behind`. The step body exists but the gate logic is wrong, so the requirement — "verify the dispatched SHA against the stable branch" — is not satisfied: the verification answers the opposite question.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:112-117 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The logic to verify the dispatched commit SHA is reversed; it allows commits ahead of the stable branch tip and rejects commits that are ancestors.
  WHY: The GitHub compare API status 'ahead' means the dispatched SHA is ahead of the stable tip (not an ancestor). The 'behind' status means the dispatched SHA is an ancestor of the stable tip. By accepting 'ahead' and rejecting 'behind', an attacker can supply a commit SHA that is not in stable's history, bypassing the verification.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:243-248 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Same reversed comparison logic as mark-stable.yml.
  WHY: An attacker can supply a commit SHA that is not in stable's history to trigger an unverified release.
- tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py:423-428 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test `test_release_source_verifies_dispatched_sha` encodes the same reversed logic bug.
  WHY: The test will incorrectly pass when the vulnerability is present and fail once the production code is corrected.
- tests/test_apply_analysis_on_main.py:363-365 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fallback accepts the insecure short-form comparison `!= "stable"` when the full-ref comparison is not found.
  WHY: If the primary workflow files regress to the insecure short-form comparison, this test will still pass due to the fallback.
- Requirement: Verify the dispatched SHA against the stable branch before exposing release credentials or executing checked-out code.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:65-124 and .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:195-255
  Evidence of absence: The verification logic is implemented but incorrectly inverted (comparing 'ahead' instead of 'behind'), failing to protect the release pipeline as intended.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:116-118 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `case "${COMPARE_STATUS}" in identical|ahead)` accepts a dispatched SHA that is not in stable's history and rejects one that is an ancestor of the live stable tip.
  WHY: With `DISPATCH_SHA` as base and `STABLE_TIP` as head, `behind` means the dispatched commit is an ancestor of the stable tip; the existing helper `scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:185` uses the correct `identical|behind` pattern.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:247-250 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case statement has the same compare-direction inversion as `mark-stable.yml:116-118`.
  WHY: A legitimate dispatched commit that is an ancestor of the stable tip is rejected with `RELEASE_UNTESTED_HEAD`, while a SHA ahead of stable can be accepted.
- tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py:423 and 429 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test asserts that `ahead` passes and `behind` fails, locking in the inverted behavior.
  WHY: The test will fail when the production case statement is corrected to accept `identical|behind`.
- tests/test_apply_analysis_on_main.py:362-366 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fallback accepts the short-form `!= "stable"` comparison.
  WHY: The assertion accepts both forms, so reintroducing the shell-injectable short form does not fail this gate.
- Requirement: "Verify the dispatched SHA against the stable branch before exposing release credentials or executing checked-out code." (linked issue #6546 recommendation)
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml source job verify step (lines 65-124) and .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml source job verify step (lines 195-255)
  Evidence of absence: Both verify steps exist and call the compare API, but the case statement at line 117 / line 248 accepts `ahead` (commit not in stable history) and rejects `behind` (commit in stable history). The verification step is implemented but inverted: it accepts SHAs that the issue requires it to reject and rejects SHAs that the issue requires it to accept. The deliverable is therefore not actually met.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
